strategy.summary: Reproduce xr.polyval returning a large negative sentinel (-1.84467441e+19, the int64-minimum NaT cast to float) instead of NaN at a NaT position in a timedelta64[D] offset array; the developer test test_polyval_timedelta_nat should fail on the buggy commit 5c1ff1cb2e3c (np.isnan(actual.values[1]) is False) and pass after the fix that masks NaT back to NaN in to_floatable.

pip_packages: xarray (checked out at buggy commit 5c1ff1cb2e3c, installed editable)
pinned_because: numpy 2.4.6 is the version reported in issue #11462 Environment section; the evidence states no documented constraint for numpy, so this pin is a reporter-observed version, not a documented requirement
python_version is not stated by the evidence and is left null; use a Python version compatible with the checked-out xarray and numpy 2.4.6

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 5c1ff1cb2e3c the test fails: xr.polyval returns -1.84467441e+19 at index 1, so np.isnan(actual.values[1]) is False and the AssertionError is raised. On the fixed revision (with to_floatable applying .where(x.notnull()) after astype(float)) the test passes: index 1 is NaN and indices [0, 2] are finite.
strategy.numerical_probe: xr.polyval(xr.DataArray(np.array([0, 'NaT', 2], dtype='timedelta64[D]'), dims='x'), xr.DataArray([2.0, 1.0], dims='degree', coords={'degree': [1, 0]})).values

input_output_examples.input: offset = xr.DataArray(np.array([0, "NaT", 2], dtype="timedelta64[D]"), dims="offset"); coefficients = xr.DataArray([2.0, 1.0], dims="degree", coords={"degree": [1, 0]}); result = xr.polyval(offset, coefficients)

risks: The reported environment lists xarray 2026.7.0 and numpy 2.4.6; the sentinel depends on plain astype(float) of the int64-minimum NaT on this numpy version. If the installed numpy differs in NaT-to-float casting, the buggy sentinel may not appear and the test may not fail on buggy.
NaT is not an IEEE special value; the bug is a sentinel from integer-minimum casting, so it will not reproduce with inf, signed zero or subnormal inputs.
The test uses np.isnan checks with no numeric tolerance; the pass/fail transition depends only on NaN presence at index 1 and finiteness at indices 0 and 2.
The regression was introduced by PR #6599 per the issue; checking out an older commit would not be the buggy revision, so use 5c1ff1cb2e3c exactly.
The PR date is blank in the context, so the exact main-branch state around the bug is not confirmed beyond the buggy commit hash.
No platform or sanitiser requirement is stated in the evidence; the behaviour is assumed platform-independent on 64-bit int64 timedelta casting.

oracle.reference_source: PR #11478 test assertion using np.isnan on actual.values[1] and on actual.values[[0, 2]]
oracle.why: The test asserts NaN presence and absence rather than numeric closeness, so the oracle is an exact NaN check.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy commit the value at index 1 is -1.84467441e+19 (the int64-minimum NaT cast to float), so np.isnan returns False and the assertion np.isnan(actual.values[1]) raises AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After the to_floatable change, astype(float) is followed by .where(x.notnull()), so index 1 becomes NaN and indices 0 and 2 remain finite, satisfying both assertions.
